answer: Agents may wander freely through a market, but access to its oasis of paid jobs requires each identity to lock 100 opal tokens as collateral for 30 days. A contract confiscates that bond if the agent submits a result that fails a predefined, verifiable check. Creating 1,000 identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens, and fraudulent submissions risk losing those funds. New names cannot erase the cost because each must post a fresh bond.
